name: hashfuncs
description: Compute non-cryptographic hashes in DuckDB with xxHash, MurmurHash3, RapidHash, wyhash, komihash, SipHash, CRC-32C and FNV-1a, and reproduce BigQuery, Spark, Kafka, Iceberg and ClickHouse hashes. Use them for partitioning, row keys, cache keys, and filter inputs.

cta.title: Fast Hashing in SQL
cta.description: Install Hashfuncs to plug industry-standard non-cryptographic hashes into DuckDB queries. For digests, signatures, or anything adversarial, use the [crypto](/products/extensions/crypto) extension instead.

quickStart.title: Assign keys to hash partitions
quickStart.description: Hash each sample key with the same seed and map it to one of four partition numbers.
quickStart.sql:
WITH users(user_id) AS (VALUES ('alice'), ('bob'), ('carol'))
SELECT user_id, xxh3_64(user_id, 42) % 4 AS partition_id
FROM users
ORDER BY user_id;
quickStart.note: Keep the algorithm, input type, and seed consistent wherever you compute the partition. These hashes are not suitable for passwords or message authentication.

introduction.title: Create repeatable hash values for data processing
paragraphs: Hashfuncs exposes named non-cryptographic algorithms such as xxHash, MurmurHash, and RapidHash. They turn a value into a fixed-size number that can be used to assign partitions, construct lookup keys, or compare fingerprints across systems.

Choose a specific algorithm, seed, and input representation when another program must reproduce the result. Hash collisions are possible, so an equal hash alone does not establish that two records are equal. For cryptographic digests or HMACs, use [Crypto](/products/extensions/crypto/).
